name: China
definition: China is the world’s largest manufacturing economy and a central node in global trade, technology supply chains, and the market for industrial demand.
happening: Policy is prioritizing advanced manufacturing and strategic autonomy while domestic demand remains uneven. Export competitiveness is rising in clean technology and machinery, widening trade friction with major partners.
why: China changes the marginal price of goods, the structure of supply chains, and the bargaining power of technology platforms. It is both a growth question and a source of regime-level tail risk.
risk: An escalation in trade restrictions or a disorderly property deleveraging could transmit through commodities, industrial earnings, and cross-border capital flows.

timeline.event: Property adjustment becomes the central drag
